t_payout.text: F3 · Step 5: payouts with Stripe Connect

n_payout.text: Sequence: GET /connect/status → 404 means no account: Payouts — not started (never the error). Continue to Stripe → POST /connect/account (Idempotency-Key) → POST /connect/onboarding-link → open it. 409 STEP_NOT_AVAILABLE → not available yet; a 5xx on account creation → couldn't set up. Requirements: a count ('Stripe needs 2 more things from you'), then a visible 'What Stripe needs' list straight under it, needed now first and needed later after. Each row is the server's label for a Stripe requirement key (Needs API: the contract forbids the app from paraphrasing Stripe). Past due says the deadline has passed ('Stripe needed this by …'); a future deadline is only for currently_due. Continue to Stripe is the footer primary. 'For support' holds only 'Copy details for support', which puts the raw keys on the clipboard; raw keys never show. Stripe still checking: 'We'll let you know when Stripe finishes' (connect.requirements_changed → rider push and email; the screen updates on open). Owner decision: when Stripe restricts an approved rider's payouts, the rider keeps taking offers and earnings go out on the next Monday payout once Stripe is fixed; this covers only riders whose payouts worked before (Payouts — paused by Stripe). The contract still blocks going online without payouts_enabled: Needs API.

n_status.text: Term: 'Account paused'. The reason comes from blocking_reasons: DOCUMENT_EXPIRED (with the EXPIRED KycDocument and valid_until) → Paused — document expired; ACCOUNT_NOT_ACTIVE alone → facts only, no Why. Owner decisions: a paused or closed rider finishes the delivery they are on unless HalalGoes contacts them (operations may move it to another rider), gets no new offers, and money already earned is always paid out, so every paused and closed screen says so. A Stripe payout restriction no longer pauses the account (the rider keeps taking offers), so Paused — payouts incomplete is removed. An admin's own reason is Needs API (alternative). Earnings answers 403 ACCOUNT_NOT_ACTIVE while paused (Paused — Earnings). No socket event carries account_status: a closed account shows the closed alert on the next 403 or /riders/me refetch, then Account closed, only when RiderMe.active_assignment_id is null. During an active delivery it shows Account closed — during a delivery (Back to delivery); sign-out waits until the assignment ends. Finishing a delivery while paused or closed also needs the rider spec's 403 rule to allow the in-flight assignment (Needs API). Expired insurance: add it (Added), Send for review, then in review; that screen updates when a person decides; a single document sends no push, but reinstating the account does (owner decision). Slate, never red.

t_account.text: F15 · Account: overview, details, terms, payouts, sign out

n_account.text: One status line under the name ('Approved · can go online'). Your details shows RiderMe fields only (name, mobile, time zone); date of birth and email are the tagged alternative. Help is the same Call support ghost button with support_hours under it. Terms and privacy: read the terms again at any time; the accepted version and date are a tagged alternative. Payouts show only ConnectStatus. Sign out: Modal confirm, focus on Cancel. Delete account sits under Terms and privacy and opens Delete account — by request (owner decision); Signed-in devices is gone (a later-version contract call).

n_account_docs.text: Replacing a document: the rider spec keeps an ACTIVE rider ONLINE-capable while a replacement is reviewed, as long as the current one hasn't expired. The confirm, the in-review alert and the Account overview status line all say so. attachRiderDocument marks the earlier row Replaced at once; the 'stays valid until approved' version stays a tagged alternative. A replacement turned down shows the reviewer note and the remedy. Owner decision: the rider keeps riding until the current document expires and is asked for a new upload; the expiry date still takes them offline if it lapses. Upload errors while replacing: too small, over 15 MB, link expired. A replacement reads Added until Send for review (submitRiderDocuments, Needs API after approval); sending, the 429 limit and 422 too-soon are drawn.

t_account_vehicle.text: F15 · Account: vehicle (change is Needs API)

n_account_vehicle.text: Changing vehicle after approval is Needs API: the contract's vehicle call is an onboarding step. Primary today: a read-only vehicle summary with 'Call support to change your vehicle'. The tagged flow opens the form first; the destructive confirm comes on Save vehicle and names both vehicles; backing out before saving changes nothing. Motorised form, PLATE_IN_USE, FIELD_REQUIRED and year range drawn for when the API lands.

t_account_delete.text: F15 · Account: delete account — by request at launch, in the app later

n_account_delete.text: Owner decision: at launch an account is deleted on request by phone or email (Delete account — by request). Account's 'Delete account' row opens it; Email support needs a support email address in PublicConfig (Needs API). In-app deletion stays in a later version and ships before the store release: the six 'Later version' boards keep that flow (explain, confirm, deleting, failed, on a delivery, done), each with its blue Needs API tag. The record retention period is still an open owner decision, so the retention line is a placeholder. Delete is a destructive tertiary button, never the orange primary; the confirm's initial focus is Keep my account. On a delivery: finish it first. Money already earned is always paid out (owner decision).

n_light.text: Owner decision: the rider app follows the phone's light or dark setting; there is no in-app theme switch. Every light board uses the same generator as its dark twin, so copy and structure match (Apply to ride — start has no consent checkbox and five steps). Light covers vehicle, capture and account documents too.

n_a11y.text: 200% text (simulated by doubling the type tokens): the body scrolls, the footer stays pinned, button labels wrap inside taller buttons and never truncate (every type token doubled, the ones DS components read too), rows wrap and the Add button drops below the text. Keyboard open: the footer rides above the keyboard and the focused field scrolls into view above it (WCAG 2.4.11).

n_ref.text: Legend: purple = Component gap (a missing size or prop on an existing design-system component) or Proposed component (a composite built from library parts and design-system components, waiting for owner approval; drawn with design-system tokens because the canvas can mount only the design-system bundle). Blue = Needs API (the contract lacks it). Grey = Data (bound to a contract field, never hardcoded) or an annotation of behaviour and screen-reader text. The boards render the installed design system as published, with no local token overrides. Orange primary button: dark label, accent-800 on brand-500 at 4.63:1. Owner decision: the rider 7:1 target covers body text, not large bold button labels, which meet 4.5:1. Where a design-system part still falls short (field helper and error text, DateInput sub-field invalid, button label wrap at 200% text) it is drawn as the system ships it with a purple Component gap tag, and listed in Reference — contract gaps.
